entities.summary:
Sancia of Majorca, also known as Sancha, was Queen of Naples from 1309 until 1343 as the wife of Robert the Wise. She served as regent of Naples during the minority of her step-granddaughter, Joanna I of Naples, from 1343 until 1344.


Sancia's reign was marked by her efforts to strengthen the kingdom's economy and promote the arts. She encouraged the establishment of trade guilds and supported the construction of new buildings in Naples. Additionally, Sancia played a key role in the development of the University of Naples, which became a center of learning and intellectual inquiry.


Sancia's legacy extends beyond her own reign, as she paved the way for future generations of female leaders in Naples. Her efforts to promote education and economic development had a lasting impact on the city and its people.


In the end, Sancia's life was cut short when she died on July 28, 1345, at the age of unknown. Despite this tragic end, her memory lived on, and she remained a beloved figure in the history of Naples.
